planted.case: the linear-kernel solve equals FoldSolver at the 11 shared penalties
a non-linear code: the kernel decoder reads it, the linear one does not
lost information: neither decoder reads more than the token holds
a token that holds only time: its kernel score against the clock floor (recorded)

rule.scores: per encoder, window part, body, target and decoder: the decoder's best cross-validated content score (1 - squared error / squared deviation of the part's target about its mean; 0 = no better than the part's mean target, 1 = exact)
rule.ruled_parts: the 4 parts of window 484,675 and parts 2-4 of window 489,350 (its part 1 shares 265 of its 300 samples with window 484,675's part 4 and is left out by encoder_check.excluded_parts): 7 parts, body 1's lower trunk at -142 to -166 degrees
rule.paired_difference: the later encoder's score minus the earlier encoder's, per ruled part, per body
rule.lower: body 1 reads LOWER under a decoder and target when encoder_check's question-1 rule (rule_reading) on its 7 paired differences reads 'later encoder lower' (lower on at least 6 of 7 AND the 97.5% upper bound of the mean paired difference, t with 6 degrees of freedom, below 0) AND its mean paired difference is below the lowest of bodies 2-8's mean paired differences (the reference band: bodies 2-8 read the same way)
rule.unreadable: linear: a ruled part's best at either end of its penalty grid for either encoder (encoder_check.curve_rule); kernel: a ruled part's best at either end of K_LAMS or at the smallest c (the most local kernel) for either encoder. A kernel best at the largest c (the smoothest kernel, nearest a low-order polynomial ridge whose linear limit the linear decoder reads) is read and counted
rule.clock: the clock clause: body 1's kernel score with the later encoder above the clock floor (the encoder-free kernel decoder on the samples' time index, same part, body and target) on at least 6 of the 7 ruled parts
rule.primary: model@489350 against model@481800 (the last encoder before the loss's onset; the trajectory row's and MECHANISM.md's reference)
reading: PREMISE: the linear decoder reads body 1 LOWER on world_posture (the registered loss reproduced against 481,800). If not: 'premise not reproduced' and nothing below is read.

LOST INFORMATION: the kernel decoder also reads body 1 LOWER on world_posture. Then: kernel LOWER on heading_free_posture = 'lost posture information' (the body's configuration); kernel not LOWER on heading_free_posture but LOWER on heading = 'lost heading'; neither = 'lost, not attributed to configuration or heading'.

NON-LINEAR CODE (no information lost): the kernel decoder does not read body 1 LOWER on world_posture (within its spread across parts, within bodies 2-8's band, or higher) AND the clock clause holds on world_posture.
NOT DECIDED BY THE TOKEN: the kernel decoder does not read body 1 LOWER on world_posture but the clock clause fails (the kernel score does not exceed what the samples' time alone gives).
UNREADABLE: the linear or the kernel reading on world_posture is unreadable (a best at a grid end, above).
rule.beside: the same rule for model@489350 against frozen@481100 and against model@484675, model@484675 against model@481800, model@481800 against frozen@481100; the rule on each ruled window alone (its 4 parts); window 479,350 (the turn from -77 to -134 degrees): whole-window and per-part scores per encoder; the best of the two decoders per reading; all deciding nothing
rule.consequence: LOST INFORMATION: a defect to repair; the separating run from 481,800 (the review's computation 3) decides its cause. NON-LINEAR CODE: no posture information lost on these rows; the loss lives in the linear read-out only, and the separating run is not needed for an information defect

outcome_rule.question: was the 481,800 configuration change (finger_joint_servo on, hand_response_calibration replaced, saved hand choice record replaced) needed for body 1's lost posture information in the span 481,800 to 484,675?
outcome_rule.primary: sibling@484675 against model@481800 on body 1's 7 ruled parts (the same rows as the info row: window 484,675's 4 parts and window 489,350's parts 2-4), under RULE's LOWER test (question-1 rule 'later encoder lower': lower on at least 6 of 7 and the 97.5% upper bound of the mean paired difference below 0, AND the mean below the lowest of bodies 2-8's means)
outcome_rule.d_sibling: body 1's mean paired kernel world-posture difference, sibling@484675 minus model@481800, 7 ruled parts
outcome_rule.d_seg41j: body 1's mean paired kernel world-posture difference, model@484675 (seg41j) minus model@481800, the same 7 parts, measured in this run (the info row read -0.101)
outcome_rule.outcome_a: (a) CONFIGURATION CHANGE NOT NEEDED IN THIS SPAN: the kernel decoder reads the sibling LOWER on world posture AND LOWER on heading-free posture (RULE's 'lost posture information' clauses) AND d_sibling <= 0.5 x d_seg41j (a change at least half of seg41j's 484,675 change; d_seg41j < 0). LOWER includes 'outside bodies 2-8's band' (below their lowest mean)
outcome_rule.outcome_b: (b) CONFIGURATION CHANGE IMPLICATED IN THIS SPAN: d_sibling lies within bodies 2-8's band of the same comparison (between the lowest and the highest of bodies 2-8's mean paired kernel world-posture differences, sibling@484675 minus model@481800), and (a) does not hold
outcome_rule.outcome_c: (c) NEITHER: anything else, said plainly with the clause that failed (e.g. LOWER but less than half of seg41j's change; below the band but the rule within the spread; LOWER on world posture but not on heading-free posture; above the band; unreadable: a kernel best at a grid end on a ruled part for either encoder of the primary pair or of seg41j's change)
outcome_rule.linear_premise_note: RULE's PREMISE clause (the linear decoder LOWER) is not part of (a): on seg41j's own 481,800 to 484,675 change the info row read the linear decoder 'within the spread' (bound +0.028) while the kernel decoder read LOWER (-0.101), so requiring it of the sibling would ask more of it than seg41j showed. RULE's full reading (decide(), premise included) is recorded beside for every pair.
beside: model@484675 (seg41j) against sibling@484675 on the same 7 parts: the rule's reading and the mean paired difference (negative = seg41j's encoder holds less than the sibling's on the same rows)

the sibling's own window (its 4 parts, its world's rows): every pair's rule on those 4 parts (3 of 4 lower and t with 3 degrees of freedom), and per part the largest row difference from window 484,675's rows at the same trainer labels (0 = the same rows, saved before the branch at 481,800)

HEADINGS: body 1's lower-trunk heading (circular mean and spread, degrees, direction_probe.heading_deg) per part of every window, both runs; a part of the sibling's window is MATCHED to the same-label part of window 484,675 when their circular means differ by no more than the larger of the two spreads; on matched parts: each 484,675 encoder on its own run's rows minus model@481800 on the same rows (kernel and linear, world posture), and the sibling encoder minus model@481800 on seg41j's rows
the frozen 481,100 encoder against the sibling; the info row's 5 pairs (reproduced)
outcome_rule.consequence: (a): candidate 3 (the configuration change) is not needed for the loss in 481,800 to 484,675; the push and the other lessons on the new heading remain, and the separating arm with --proprio-token-skip 1,3 (no push on body 1) separates them. (b): candidate 3 is implicated in this span; one arm each, so the arms' other differences stay beside it: body 1 pushed at 5 of 29 trainer records in seg41j against 3 of 29 in the sibling, and the worlds' drift (the heading table). (c): reported with its numbers; the coordinator decides the next separating step.
